hypothesis: On two registered min-internal=3 EML targets that differ in truncated Gibbs mass Φ, master-formula GD recovery rates differ if fiber mass governs access. Equal rates reject Φ-predicts-GD at this bound. The process is GD on a master formula, not a Gibbs sampler.

controls.description: Both headline skeletons have three internal nodes and four learnable 1-leaves. Min-size cannot rank them.
The fat target is the algebraic zero identity. The singleton is the nonzero constant e-ln(e-1).
Search is hand-derived GD on a known size-3 master skeleton, not a draw from the census.
Near-true all-ones weights on the zero skeleton must recover MSE < 1e-6 or the claim is withheld.
The ranking rule is frozen before blind counts. Equal rates reject Φ-predicts-GD. Do not dress a null as a win.
The run must not claim Odrzywołek's neural bootstrap.

gates.criterion: Both headline trees have min_internal 3; zero is 0 on the grid; singleton is not 0; the x-zero identity also holds.
The summary states GD on a master formula, not tree sampling.
Replaying the registered seeds yields the same success counts.
The preregistered two-sided rule is applied and recorded. It is not chosen from the counts.
The run does not claim Odrzywołek's neural bootstrap.
At least one near-true init on the zero skeleton recovers MSE < 1e-6. Failure withholds, and does not reject Φ.
